says: In next/, the transport's WebCrypto stand-in builds its own pair of Proxy objects with a hand-written bound-member reader, beside @kampus/vitest's Stub.make, which its own doc and PR 1481 name the one stand-in for a platform object, so the tree now shows agents two ways to stand in for a platform object.
proof: next/packages/vitest/src/Stub.ts:2 reads 'The one stand-in for a platform object (decision 0554)', and next/packages/vitest/src/index.ts exports it as Stub; next/packages/libfabrika/src/transport/internal/rejecting.test-support.ts:592 and :595 each write `new Proxy(...)` for crypto.subtle and crypto, with its own `bound` helper at :577. Stub.make was on the tests step's base (9598eee is an ancestor of d1ba73ef2).
cost: Agents copy what they read (0562): a second stand-in shape spreads, and 0557's rule that a needed test mechanism is built in the test package gets a counterexample. Wrapping a real object (bind each member, change one) is not what Stub.make does today, so the fix is either Stub.make grows that case or this file is recorded as the reason it cannot.
